# BLO-32734 — scope the shared data PVC per company with nested subPath mounts

Tracking: [BLO-32734](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-32734) · PR: [#1820](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/1820)

Recorded here rather than in `PROVENANCE-CHANGES.md`: that file is frozen (BLO-34872) because concurrent appends to it conflict on GitHub's server-side merge and get ejected from the merge queue.

## 1. Initial change

**Files:** `src/server/job-manifest.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`, `src/server/execute.ts`, `src/server/k8s-client.ts`, `src/server/execute.test.ts`, `src/server/execute-environment.test.ts`, `src/server/job-adopt.test.ts`, `src/server/secret-adopt.test.ts`

Scoped the shared data PVC per company. The `data` volume was mounted **whole with no `subPath`** on both containers, and every agent pod runs as `uid=1000(node)`, so any pod could read **and write** every other company's run logs, workspaces, instruction bundles and the fleet-shared `.claude/` hook surface — a cross-tenant code-execution path, not merely a confidentiality one. `chmod`/`chown`/POSIX ACLs cannot fix it (one uid), so the remedy is a mount change: the broad mount becomes `readOnly` and `resolveScopedWritableMounts()` re-opens exactly the trees this run needs as nested rw `subPath` mounts, derived **from the runtime isolation descriptor itself** so the mount set and the descriptor cannot disagree, with a fail-closed containment guard (under `dataMountPath`, no `..`, and never the data root itself). The narrowing is applied only when the server can pre-create the targets: without `fsGroup` the kubelet creates a missing `subPath` dir `root:root 0755`, which is EACCES for uid 1000, and `fsGroup: 1000` is deliberately NOT used because on a whole-volume mount it recursively chowns ~1.5 TB of CephFS on every pod start. `SELF_POD_DATA_MOUNT_PATH` is exported from `k8s-client.ts` because those pre-create paths must be addressed through the **server's** mount of the volume, never the pod's — joining them onto `dataMountPath` would, under a custom `workspaceMountPath`, mkdir on the server's own root filesystem and leave the Job's volume untouched. Any run that cannot be scoped keeps today's broad rw mount and **names the reason** in an annotation rather than silently presenting as isolated. Two follow-ups from the Ally review of [#1820](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/1820). (a) The four test files that `vi.mock("./k8s-client.js", () => ({...}))` are converted to `importOriginal` partial mocks: a whole-module replacement silently drops every export the module later gains, which is how adding `SELF_POD_DATA_MOUNT_PATH` broke 4 tests in `execute.test.ts`, and is the third time that trap has fired in this directory (`prompt-cache.js` on [#1669](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/1669), `server-utils` before it). (b) `buildPodLogPath()` hardcoded `/paperclip`, so under a custom `workspaceMountPath` the pod log had **four consumers split across two address spaces that disagreed**: `resolveScopedWritableMounts()` skipped the log dir as off-volume (leaving the `tee` writing under the now-read-only mount) while the container's `mkdir`/`tee` addressed a path that is not the PVC mount in the Job at all — logs land on the container filesystem and vanish with the pod, and the server-side `podLogPath` used for tailing and final capture never appears. The function now takes a `root`, defaulting to the server's mount because every caller outside this module is server-side; the single call site derives both views from it, and a new test pins all four consumers to one volume under `/srv/agent-data` with each guard separately mutation-tested.

## 2. Ally review follow-ups

**Files:** `src/server/job-manifest.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`, `src/server/execute.ts`, `src/server/k8s-client.ts`, `src/server/execute.test.ts`, `src/server/execute-environment.test.ts`, `src/server/job-adopt.test.ts`, `src/server/secret-adopt.test.ts`

The narrowing is applied only when the server can pre-create the targets: without `fsGroup` the kubelet creates a missing `subPath` dir `root:root 0755`, which is EACCES for uid 1000, and `fsGroup: 1000` is deliberately NOT used because on a whole-volume mount it recursively chowns ~1.5 TB of CephFS on every pod start. `SELF_POD_DATA_MOUNT_PATH` is exported from `k8s-client.ts` because those pre-create paths must be addressed through the **server's** mount of the volume, never the pod's — joining them onto `dataMountPath` would, under a custom `workspaceMountPath`, mkdir on the server's own root filesystem and leave the Job's volume untouched. Two follow-ups from the Ally review of [#1820](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/1820). (a) The four test files that `vi.mock("./k8s-client.js", () => ({...}))` are converted to `importOriginal` partial mocks: a whole-module replacement silently drops every export the module later gains, which is how adding `SELF_POD_DATA_MOUNT_PATH` broke 4 tests in `execute.test.ts`, and is the third time that trap has fired in this directory (`prompt-cache.js` on [#1669](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/1669), `server-utils` before it). (b) `buildPodLogPath()` hardcoded `/paperclip`, so under a custom `workspaceMountPath` the pod log had **four consumers split across two address spaces that disagreed**: `resolveScopedWritableMounts()` skipped the log dir as off-volume (leaving the `tee` writing under the now-read-only mount) while the container's `mkdir`/`tee` addressed a path that is not the PVC mount in the Job at all — logs land on the container filesystem and vanish with the pod, and the server-side `podLogPath` used for tailing and final capture never appears. The function now takes a `root`, defaulting to the server's mount because every caller outside this module is server-side; the single call site derives both views from it, and a new test pins all four consumers to one volume under `/srv/agent-data` with each guard separately mutation-tested. (c) A third Ally review caught the same class arriving from the OTHER side: this narrowing now governs **which paths on this volume are writable at all**, so every producer of a path on the data PVC has to be wired into `resolveScopedWritableMounts()` or it silently lands read-only. BLO-36583 (the row directly above) added the shared pnpm store a week earlier; the two changes never touch the same lines, so `git rebase` replayed cleanly and had nothing to say about the coverage gap. `PNPM_HOME` pointed at `.../k8s-isolation/pnpm/${companyId}`, a **sibling** of the isolation root rather than a descendant of any derived candidate, so on the dominant configuration (`narrowWritableSurface` requires `isolation.enabled`, and every non-ephemeral workspace is `storage.workspace: "persistent"`) every `pnpm` write would have hit EROFS — including the `mkdir` of a store that does not exist yet for most companies. It is now a derived candidate, which makes server-side pre-creation free via `scopedWritableDirs`, and `SHARED_PNPM_STORE_ROOT` became a root-relative subpath so the store follows `dataMountPath` — the same two-address-space fix as (b), applied to the one other path in this file that hardcoded `/paperclip`. **The rule for the next path added to this volume: a path is not on the PVC because it is spelled `/paperclip/...`; it is on it when a derived writable mount covers it.**

## 3. Fourth Ally review

**Files:** `src/server/job-manifest.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`

Fourth Ally review pass on [#1820](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/1820), and the same two-address-space defect as (b) and (c) in the row above — this time in the isolation roots themselves. `resolveJobIsolation()`'s **config-source** default hardcoded `/paperclip/instances/default/data/k8s-isolation/...`, so under a custom `config.workspaceMountPath` all of `homeRoot`/`sessionRoot`/`workspaceRoot`/`cacheRoot`/`tmpRoot` addressed a directory that is **not a mount in that pod at all**: `HOME`, `workingDir` and the init container's `mkdir -p` landed on the container filesystem and vanished at pod exit, while the off-volume filter in `resolveScopedWritableMounts()` skipped every one of them with no error — so the emitted writable set reduced to the pod log dir, the pnpm store and the two scratch mounts. The default is now derived from `resolveDataMountPath(config)`, which is the same fix `sharedPnpmStorePath` and `buildPodLogPath` already carry. A **runtime**-source descriptor's roots are server-supplied and cannot be derived, so that half is reported instead: a root the descriptor declares `storage: persistent` while placing it outside the data mount now emits `claude_k8s.isolation_root_off_volume`, following the precedent `resolveLinkedWorktreeCommonDir` set — the run proceeds narrowed and fails later somewhere unrelated, which is unreadable without it. The warning is gated on `persistent` deliberately: a runtime descriptor puts `cacheRoot`/`tmpRoot` on the `/runtime-cache` emptyDir by design, and a warning that fires on the normal path is one everybody learns to skip. Three new tests, each guard separately mutation-tested (reverting the derivation, removing the warn call, and dropping the `persistent` gate each turn the suite red on its own). Also corrects the `persistent`-gate comment on the pnpm candidate: it justified itself with *“cacheRoot is off-volume”*, which holds for these fixtures and the config-source default but is not a property of the type — nothing stops a runtime descriptor putting `cacheRoot` on the PVC, and what actually makes that case safe is that `cacheRoot` is a derived candidate in its own right. **Known residual, filed separately: `promptCacheRoot` is the one root with a server-side writer** (`prepareClaudePromptBundle` writes the skills bundle in the paperclip process, then the pod reads the same absolute path via `--add-dir`/`--append-system-prompt-file`), so it needs the bundle to return both addresses rather than one — out of scope here and unchanged by this commit.

## 4. Fifth Ally review — scratch-remap rollout note

**Files:** `src/server/job-manifest.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`

**Rollout note — pre-existing `/paperclip/work` and `/paperclip/wt` scratch becomes invisible to scoped pods on deploy. This is accepted, not a bug.** `SCRATCH_DIR_NAMES` re-mounts those two trees at the same path with a company-scoped `subPath`, so a `narrowWritableSurface` run sees `work/<companyId>` where it used to see the flat shared tree. The docblock justified this on writes only — an agent writing `/paperclip/work/foo` verbatim still lands in its own subdir — and was silent on **reads of data already there**, which is the half that breaks. Measured on the live volume 2026-10-05: `work` holds 2657 entries and `wt` holds 161, **none** company-prefixed (`ls | grep -cE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-'` → 0 in both), and `work/<companyId>`/`wt/<companyId>` do not exist for any company yet, so the first scoped run of every company gets an empty directory.

Disposition: **accept the break and document it** rather than migrate or dual-mount. (a) A migration is not obviously possible — the entries carry no company attribution in their names, so there is nothing to sort 2657 directories by, and guessing would scatter one company's scratch across others, which is the cross-company read this PR exists to close. (b) Nothing is lost: the bytes stay at `<volume>/work/<name>` and the paperclip server, which mounts the volume whole, still reaches every one of them — so recovery is a server-side copy into `work/<companyId>/`, not a restore. (c) A read-only `/paperclip/work-legacy` mount for one deprecation cycle was considered and rejected: it is new permanent mount surface, on every pod, to preserve agent scratch that is by definition disposable — and it re-opens cross-company **read**, which is half of what this PR closes. The expected failure report is "my scratch vanished"; this note is here so it resolves in one read instead of becoming an incident.

The `SCRATCH_DIR_NAMES` docblock now states the read break and points here. It also records that the scoping is **inert wherever a deeper derived candidate covers the same subtree** — the kubelet orders mounts by depth, so a runtime descriptor placing a workspace under `/paperclip/wt/...` re-exposes that subtree unscoped. That is correct (the descriptor is the authority on where the data lives) but it means these two names are scoped by default, not unconditionally, and the previous wording implied the latter.

The review's defence-in-depth suggestion — have the scoped-mount append site consult `claimedMountPaths` — is **declined, because the hazard is already caught and the codebase has an explicit decision against this shape.** The suggestion is right that a derived candidate or scratch path landing exactly on an inherited secret mount under the data mount would produce two `volumeMounts` at one path. But the per-container duplicate-`mountPath` assertion at the end of `buildJobManifest` already rejects it, for both the main and init lists, with a message that names both volumes and the container — strictly more informative than what an append-site check would say. That assertion's own comment states the rule being proposed against: *"assert the invariant per container rather than trusting each append site to remember it."* A check in the scoped loop is the second copy of the condition it was written to avoid. Verified empirically rather than argued: with an append-site throw temporarily added and then neutered, the collision still failed closed via the downstream assertion. What was genuinely missing is **coverage**, not a guard — nothing exercised a scoped mount colliding with an inherited secret mount. One test now does, and it is mutation-checked: neutering the downstream assertion turns it red on its own. A second test pinning "nesting under the data mount stays legal" was written and then deleted as redundant — `still allows a NESTED workspace mount path — only exact duplicates are illegal` already covers that, which a prefix-check mutation confirmed. The append site carries a comment saying why it has no check of its own.

## 5. Linear re-cut onto master — scoped mounts emitted parent-first

**Files:** `src/server/job-manifest.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`

Master gained the BLO-40401 shadowing backstop while this PR sat conflicted: `buildJobManifest` now throws when a container declares a mount that is a strict parent of one declared earlier. `resolveScopedWritableMounts` emitted the sorted derived candidates first and appended the `work`/`wt` scratch mounts after them, so a derived candidate nested under a scratch tree (a workspace under `/paperclip/wt/...`, the case section 4 documents) now failed every such run at manifest construction instead of running. The re-cut applied without a textual conflict there — the two changes never touched the same lines.

The returned list is now sorted by `mountPath`, which puts every parent before its children, so the derived mount is applied over the scratch mount as the `SCRATCH_DIR_NAMES` docblock describes. The docblock and the call-site comment no longer claim the kubelet reorders mounts by depth; they state the declaration-order rule the backstop enforces. New test `emits a scratch mount before a derived candidate nested under it`, mutation-checked: dropping the sort reproduces the backstop error.
